# 1 Samuel Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 188-189 | **Source Image:** 1SA_012_page_001.jpg, 1SA_012_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And Samuel said to all Israel, "Behold, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you.
**2** And now, behold, the king walks before you, and I am old and gray-headed, and behold, my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth until this day.
**3** Here I am; testify against me before the LORD and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? Or whose donkey have I taken? Or whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Or from whose hand have I taken a bribe to blind my eyes with it? And I will restore it to you."
**4** And they said, "You have not defrauded us, and you have not oppressed us, and you have not taken anything from the hand of any man."
**5** And he said to them, "The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that you have not found anything in my hand." And they said, "He is witness."
**6** And Samuel said to the people, "It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron and who brought your fathers up from the land of Egypt.
**7** Now therefore, stand still, and I will judge with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD that he did with you and with your fathers.
**8** When Jacob came to Egypt, your fathers cried out to the LORD, and the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, and they brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
**9** But they forgot the LORD their God, and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
**10** And they cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. And now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.'
**11** And the LORD sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and he delivered you from the hand of your enemies on every side, and you dwelt in safety.
**12** And when you saw that Nahash the king of the sons of Ammon came against you, you said to me, 'No, but a king shall reign over us' — when the LORD your God was your king.
**13** And now, behold the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked for. And behold, the LORD has set a king over you.
**14** If you will fear the LORD and serve him and listen to his voice and not rebel against the mouth of the LORD, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be after the LORD your God.
**15** But if you will not listen to the voice of the LORD, and you rebel against the mouth of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you and against your fathers.
**16** Now also, stand still and see this great thing that the LORD is about to do before your eyes.
**17** Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, and he will send thunder and rain, and you shall know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the eyes of the LORD, in asking for yourselves a king."
**18** And Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD sent thunder and rain on that day, and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.
**19** And all the people said to Samuel, "Pray to the LORD your God on behalf of your servants, that we may not die, for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for ourselves a king."
**20** And Samuel said to the people, "Do not fear. You have done all this evil, yet do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
**21** And do not turn aside after the empty things that cannot profit and cannot deliver, for they are emptiness.
**22** For the LORD will not abandon his people, for the sake of his great name, because the LORD has been pleased to make you a people for himself.
**23** Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. And I will instruct you in the good and upright way.
**24** Only fear the LORD and serve him in truth with all your heart, for see what great things he has done for you.
**25** But if you indeed do evil, both you and your king will be swept away."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agreed on the verse count (25 verses) and narrative structure for this chapter. SOPHIA follows the LOGOS formal-equivalence rendering as the baseline consensus, adopting PNEUMA's phrasing where it demonstrably improves clarity without sacrificing accuracy. Key terms and theological vocabulary were consistently rendered across all three translations.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 1
- **EMET:** "And-said Samuel to all Israel, "Behold, I-have-listened to-your-voice in-all that you-said to-me, and-I-have-made-king over-you a-king."
- **LOGOS:** "And Samuel said to all Israel, "Behold, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have made a king reign over you."
- **PNEUMA:** "Samuel addressed all Israel: "I have listened to everything you said to me, and I have set a king over you."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 2
- **EMET:** "And-now, behold, the-king walks before-you, and-I have-grown-old and-gray-headed, and-behold, my-sons [are] with-you. And-I have-walked before-you fro..."
- **LOGOS:** "And now, behold, the king walks before you, and I am old and gray-headed, and behold, my sons are with you. And I have walked before you from my youth..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Now you have a king to lead you. As for me — I am old and gray, and my sons are here among you. I have walked before you from my youth until this very..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 4
- **EMET:** "And-they-said, "You-have-not-defrauded us, and-you-have-not-oppressed us, and-you-have-not-taken from-[the]-hand of-any-man anything.""
- **LOGOS:** "And they said, "You have not defrauded us, and you have not oppressed us, and you have not taken anything from the hand of any man.""
- **PNEUMA:** "They answered, "You have not cheated us. You have not oppressed us. You have never taken anything from anyone's hand.""
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 7
- **EMET:** "And-now, stand-yourselves, and-I-will-judge with-you before YHWH [concerning] all [the]-righteous-acts of-YHWH (*tsidqot YHWH*) which he-did with-you ..."
- **LOGOS:** "Now therefore, stand still, and I will judge with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD that he did with you and with your..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Now take your stand, so I can lay before you the evidence — all the righteous acts the LORD has done for you and your ancestors."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 11
- **EMET:** "And-YHWH sent Yerub-Baal (*Jerubbaal*) and-Bedan and-Yiphtach (*Jephthah*) and-Samuel, and-he-delivered you from-[the]-hand of-your-enemies on-every-s..."
- **LOGOS:** "And the LORD sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and he delivered you from the hand of your enemies on every side, and you dwelt in safe..."
- **PNEUMA:** "So the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and he delivered you from the enemies all around you, and you lived in safety."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 13
- **EMET:** "And-now, behold the-king whom you-have-chosen, whom you-have-asked-for; and-behold, YHWH has-set over-you a-king."
- **LOGOS:** "And now, behold the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked for. And behold, the LORD has set a king over you."
- **PNEUMA:** "Now here is the king you have chosen, the one you demanded. The LORD has placed a king over you."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 15
- **EMET:** "And-if you-will-not listen to-[the]-voice of-YHWH, and-you-rebel against [the]-mouth of-YHWH, then-will-be [the]-hand of-YHWH against-you and-against ..."
- **LOGOS:** "But if you will not listen to the voice of the LORD, and you rebel against the mouth of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you and ag..."
- **PNEUMA:** "But if you do not obey the LORD's voice and instead rebel against his commands, then the LORD's hand will be against you, as it was against your ances..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 17
- **EMET:** "[Is it] not wheat-harvest today? I-will-call to YHWH, and-he-will-give thunders (*qolot*) and-rain, and-know and-see that your-evil [is] great which y..."
- **LOGOS:** "Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, and he will send thunder and rain, and you shall know and see that your evil is great, whi..."
- **PNEUMA:** "Is it not wheat harvest right now? I will call on the LORD to send thunder and rain. Then you will see and understand how great an evil you committed ..."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.
### Verse 21
- **EMET:** "And-do-not-turn-aside after the-emptiness (*tohu*) which cannot-profit and-cannot-deliver, for they [are] emptiness."
- **LOGOS:** "And do not turn aside after the empty things that cannot profit and cannot deliver, for they are emptiness."
- **PNEUMA:** "Do not turn aside after worthless things that can neither help nor rescue you, because they are nothing."
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows the LOGOS rendering as the formal-equivalence baseline, noting PNEUMA's dynamic phrasing as a valid alternative reading.

— SOPHIA
